assumptions: The evaluation treats the opportunity as competently pursued from the current discovery stage rather than penalizing it merely for lacking traction.
The founder retains a full-time job and can allocate no more than approximately 20-25 hours per week until objective traction and runway justify leaving employment.
The proposed product does not receive exclusive access to importer, supplier, broker, verifier, or regulatory data unless such rights are later contracted.
Competitor pricing and SAP's announced capabilities remain commercially available enough to constrain pricing and differentiation.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid diagnostics from several above-threshold importers, conversion into annual contracts at the proposed price, measured forecast-error or certificate-cost improvement, fully loaded onboarding and support economics, renewals, signed referral partners, and durable contractual rights to ingest and reuse permissioned data would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: CBAM converts emissions data into a mandatory, recurring certificate cash exposure, so connecting supplier evidence and customs records to treasury decisions addresses a real gap beyond compliance reporting. The insight is weakened because competitors and SAP already connect much of this workflow.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Covered declarants face a compulsory and measurable cash event, and a named importer case demonstrates real use of CBAM workflow software. However, no paid engagement, savings result, renewal, or willingness to pay at the proposed 36,000-120,000 PLN annual price has been established for this offer.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual prepayment, recurring regulatory work, and software-like delivery could support attractive cash conversion and margins. The proposed CAC, 75-85% contribution margin, onboarding burden, retention, savings, and owner-earnings path are unvalidated, while a direct substitute at €2,500 per year creates substantial pricing pressure.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market EU importers in specified CBAM sectors form an identifiable beachhead with clear triggering events. The 50-tonne threshold removes many smaller importers, the Polish addressable customer count is unknown, and larger accounts are more likely to use incumbent ERP or customs platforms.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A procurement-to-treasury focus could earn a useful vertical workflow position, but neither that position nor customer access is currently controlled. Low-priced specialist software and SAP's end-to-end offering, including planned cash-impact forecasting, make segment domination difficult without a much narrower proprietary wedge.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Success could extend across additional CBAM sectors, EU geographies, supplier evidence preparation, procurement scenarios, verifier coordination, and broader carbon-cost planning. These adjacencies become credible only after obtaining durable importer data access and proving the initial economics.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned evidence-quality benchmarks and embedded workflows could compound, but they do not yet exist and reuse rights are unknown. Core regulatory inputs are public, essential data remains externally controlled, and established ERP, customs, and ESG vendors can copy or bundle forecasting features.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cash forecasting tied to procurement decisions is potentially more actionable than reporting-only tools, but the evidence shows direct competitors already offer cost projections and procurement tools, while SAP covers the broader data and accounting workflow. No quantified improvement in exposure, accuracy, speed, or total cost has been demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime began in 2026, certificate prices are now published, and declarants face recurring purchase, verification, and surrender workflows. This creates immediate urgency, although the same timing is accelerating incumbent product launches.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs brokers and trade-finance advisers are plausible trust-bearing channels, and a paid diagnostic is a sensible entry offer. No referral agreement, qualified pipeline, conversion rate, observed sales cycle, or repeatable acquisition result supports the proposed route, and enterprise selling may strain a part-time founder.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's quantitative and data-integration skills fit the product, AI can accelerate development, and the proposed 70,000 PLN budget is within available capital. Execution still depends on enterprise security, regulatory accuracy, specialist oversight, accredited verifiers, supplier and importer cooperation, integrations, and sales effort that AI cannot remove.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the beachhead to one high-exposure importer vertical underserved by SAP, secure a customs-broker distribution partnership and standardized data access, and make the product's core promise a contractually measurable treasury outcome rather than broad CBAM compliance functionality.
main_structural_strength: A mandatory recurring certificate purchase converts regulatory compliance into a concrete treasury exposure, creating an identifiable payer, purchase trigger, and repeat workflow.
primary_score_limiter: The candidate lacks a demonstrated proprietary advantage or controlled distribution channel against low-priced specialists and ERP incumbents, while its price, savings, acquisition cost, retention, and support economics remain unvalidated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: SAP has announced an end-to-end CBAM solution spanning ERP and customs data, supplier ingestion, certificate calculations, accounting, reporting, and planned cash-impact forecasting, while Carbon Glance already advertises overlapping cost and procurement functions for €2,500 annually.
